subject: Efficient implementation of expected improvement computation in generated quantites block

messages.author: 5a363da2ae84b3c2
messages.subject: Efficient implementation of expected improvement computation in generated quantites block
parts:
I'm working on a fully Bayesian extension of Efficient Global Optimization, which builds a GP model of an expensive-to-compute surface as a way to make inferences about where the global minimum is. I believe everything prior to the generated quantities block is as efficient as is possible, and that the generated quantities block is what's slowing everything down. 

N2 is ~ 20,000 while N1 is ~ 20, so computing the matrix K has a high cost, especially since I only need the diagonal of K'*Sigma^-1*K. Since we already have the Cholesky factor L of Sigma in hand, that means K'*Sigma^-1*K = K'*L^-T*L^-1*K. Denoting for A=K'L^-T, K'*Sigma^-1*K = AA', i.e. A is a factorization of the solution we want. But I'm pretty sure this observation won't actually save me any computational effort, since it doesn't let me compute the diagonal any more quickly (and I'd still need to compute K'Sigma^-1=A*L^-1 at some point for use in ln_y2_hat).

Since each iteration takes ~2s on my computer, it has dawned on my why latin hypercube sampling is so often referenced in this literature: it reduces the number of new points to try. So if it's true that there's not a more efficient way to do this in stan for N2 of this size, it'd still be something I'd like to know!

Thanks for your time.

anisotropicRBF_fullBayes <- "
    data{
        int<lower=1> N1;
        int<lower=1> N2;
        int<lower=1> D;
        matrix[N1,D] x1;
        matrix[N2,D] x2;
        vector[N1] ln_y1;
    }
    transformed data{
        vector[N2] min_ln_y1;
        min_ln_y1 <- rep_vector(min(ln_y1),N2);
    }
    parameters{
        real<lower=0> eta_sq;
        vector<lower=0>[D] inv_rho_sq;
        real<lower=0> sigma_sq;
        real mu;
    }
    transformed parameters{
        matrix[N1,N1] L;
        vector<lower=0>[D] rho_sq;
        matrix[N1,N1] Sigma;
        matrix[D,D] rho_sq_mat;
        vector[N1] mu_vec;

        mu_vec <- rep_vector(mu, N1);

        for(d in 1:D) rho_sq[d] <- inv(inv_rho_sq[d]);

        rho_sq_mat <- diag_matrix(rho_sq);

        for(i in 1:(N1-1)){
            for(j in (i+1):N1){
                Sigma[i,j] <- eta_sq * exp( (x1[i]-x1[j]) * -rho_sq_mat * (x1[i]-x1[j])');
                Sigma[j,i] <- Sigma[i,j];                
            }
        }
        for(k in 1:N1) Sigma[k,k] <- eta_sq+sigma_sq;
        L <- cholesky_decompose(Sigma);
    }   
    model{
        eta_sq ~ cauchy(0,5);
        inv_rho_sq ~ cauchy(0,5);
        sigma_sq ~ cauchy(0,5);
        ln_y1 ~ multi_normal_cholesky(mu_vec, L);
    }
    generated quantities{
        vector[N2] ln_y2_hat;
        vector[N2] s_vec;
        vector[N2] improv;
        {
            vector[N2] Omega_diag;
            matrix[N1,N2] K;
            matrix[N2,N1] K_t_inv_Sigma;
            vector[N2] delta;

            Omega_diag <- rep_vector(eta_sq, N2);
            
            for(i in 1:N1)
                for(j in 1:N2)
                    K[i,j] <- eta_sq * exp( (x1[i]-x2[j]) * -rho_sq_mat * (x1[i]-x2[j])' );

            K_t_inv_Sigma <- K'/Sigma;
            ln_y2_hat <- rep_vector(mu, N2)+K_t_inv_Sigma*(ln_y1-mu_vec);
            s_vec <- Omega_diag-diagonal(K_t_inv_Sigma*K);
            delta <- min_ln_y1-ln_y2_hat;

            for(n in 1:N2) improv[n] <- delta[n] * normal_cdf(delta[n], 0, s_vec[n])+s_vec[n] * exp(normal_log(delta[n], 0, s_vec[n]));
        }
    }
"

messages.author: f13fe7e880ed6103
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Efficient implementation of expected improvement computation in generated quantites block
parts:
It could be a memory I/O issue--you can test this by using CmdStan instead of R, or within R you can try the pars argument, which tells stan() which parameters to save. Have you already tried just leaving out the generated quantities block to get a sense of how much time it's actually taking up? 

Happy to help debug more, but you'll need to send us some data so I can try running your model.

Seth
